exposure: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (pre-eclampsia, chronic hypertension, gestational hypertension)
blood pressure >= 140/90 mmHg at the postnatal visit
outcome: Renal dysfunction (eGFR < 60 ml/min/1.73 m2 or proteinuria > 150 mg/24h or urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio > 3 mg/mmol)
cohort: The study included 740 women (out of 1050 invited) who had a pregnancy complicated by a hypertensive disorder and attended a 6-8 weeks postpartum review at a specialist fetal-maternal medicine clinic.
finding: Renal dysfunction was present in 32% of women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy at 6-8 weeks postpartum, with pre-eclampsia, chronic hypertension, highest antenatal serum creatinine, highest antenatal urinary protein, and elevated postnatal blood pressure identified as independent predictors.
